methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective cohort is appropriate for describing rare NTRK-fusion papillary thyroid carcinoma and comparing it with a large BRAFV600E PTC group, and all included patients had preoperative FNAB with multigene testing. The NTRK cohort is small at 38 patients, follow-up is short, and the BRAFV600E comparator lacks comprehensive pathological re-review and has high loss to follow-up as acknowledged. Statistical methods are conventional and include odds ratios and ROC analysis, but most analyses are unadjusted, small subgroup comparisons are underpowered, and no multiplicity correction is reported across numerous clinicopathologic and sonographic features.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective single-center case series with comparison to a molecular comparator cohort, so Oxford level 4 is appropriate. The clinical relevance is clear because NTRK fusions are actionable alterations in thyroid carcinoma and preoperative recognition may affect risk stratification, lymph-node evaluation, and surgical planning. Relevance is limited by short follow-up, lack of treatment-response data to TRK inhibitors, and the small number of NTRK1 cases.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is applicable to this retrospective observational cohort. The manuscript reports study period, inclusion and exclusion criteria, molecular testing panel, ultrasound review process, pathological re-review for NTRK-fusion cases, follow-up schedule, and statistical tests. Reporting gaps include limited information on missing-data handling, selection effects from offering molecular testing, no multivariable model for group comparisons, no formal sample-size justification, and no open data or code availability statement in the normalized manuscript.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper provides a meaningful population and molecular-context extension by characterizing unselected, preoperatively tested NTRK-fusion PTC and comparing it with BRAFV600E PTC. Prior studies have already described NTRK-fusion thyroid carcinoma, follicular-pattern histology, younger age, and lymph-node propensity, which limits conceptual novelty. The strongest novel elements are the systematic sonographic/cytopathologic comparison and the reported tumor-size association with lateral lymph-node metastasis in this rare subgroup.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured, with results organized around NTRK fusion characteristics, NTRK1 versus NTRK3 comparisons, lateral lymph-node risk factors, BRAFV600E comparisons, and sonographic findings. The abstract is quantitatively detailed and aligned with the main text. Figure and table captions are concise but identify the content of each display, and the discussion carefully compares findings with prior cohorts while acknowledging small sample size, short follow-up, and comparator limitations.

key_strengths: Focuses on a rare but actionable molecular subtype of papillary thyroid carcinoma.
Uses preoperative FNAB-based multigene testing and includes detailed clinicopathologic, cytologic, and sonographic characterization.
Large BRAFV600E comparator cohort provides context for age, tumor size, lymph-node involvement, and imaging differences.
Identifies a clinically practical ultrasound tumor-size threshold associated with lateral lymph-node metastasis.
Discussion is well positioned against prior NTRK-fusion thyroid carcinoma literature.
key_concerns: Only 38 NTRK-fusion cases, with just 7 NTRK1 cases, limiting subgroup inference.
Retrospective single-center design with possible selection bias from molecular testing availability.
Most comparisons are unadjusted and numerous, with no multiplicity correction.
Follow-up is short and comparator follow-up/pathology re-review are limited.
No open data or analysis code is described.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a useful and well-written rare-subtype observational study with clear clinical relevance, but the small NTRK cohort and retrospective unadjusted analyses limit impact. Tier 3 with minor revisions is plausible for a specialty oncology or pathology audience.
